reachable: Yes, on both mechanisms, and both get gradient. Batcher: G.load_batcher passes the genome params, and _train calls next_batch every step, so the depth tilt and the systematic draw govern the composition of all 4000 batches — it acts on the gradient through which sequences are in the batch, which is the only channel it claims. Arch: the occlusion is inside forward under `if self.training`, so it changes the input distribution for all steps after 301 (4000-step budget, ramp 300-1000, so it is live for ~92% of training). Because the causal mask already prevents cmd_i from seeing obs_i, occluding obs_i does not corrupt its own target — the loss target tgt[i]=z_obs[i] is untouched — it removes obs_i as an input to every LATER command position, which is exactly the denoising regime claimed. The occluded steps also switch off R24's memory write (active_pair = valid_cmd & valid_obs) and zero the closure's RHS (obs_pad = obs_tok * valid_obs), while the closure's attention scores come from cmd_raw and are untouched, matching the hypothesis. One caveat the hypothesis does not state: R24 zero-initialises ref_read, so at step 0 ref_gate/ref_own/ref_q/ref_recency all have exactly zero gradient; after 3 AdamW steps they carry gradient (ref_gate 0.21, ref_own 0.022, ref_q 1.5e-3). Occlusion only starts at step 301, so the branch is warm by then — no dead-mechanism problem. Nothing here is gated on an observation being PRESENT at the read; the arch mechanism is training-only and net.eval() is called before every scoring forward (realenv/seq_worldmodel.py:271, evolve/cups_probe.py:135), so the eval path is bit-for-bit the parent's.
solves_outside_model: Clean on both axes. The batcher parses `mv`/`cp`/redirection command strings into a per-sequence longest-chain integer, but that integer is only ever used as a sampling weight and a sort key inside make_batcher: d_all feeds w = (1+d)^alpha and argsort, and next_batch returns a plain list of indices. Nothing is written into any tensor the model sees, fit is not mutated (verified: image/cmds identical after a training run), the batcher is never constructed outside evolve/harness._train, and no batcher code runs at scoring time. This is the permitted "parse commands to choose SAMPLES" kind, not the retracted "resolve routing and stamp it into the input" kind — the read token at scoring is untouched, and the stream axis is baseline_interleave. The arch mechanism removes information (zeroes and key-pads observation tokens) rather than adding any, is gated on self.training, and consumes only its own inputs — it cannot leak. Hygiene checks pass: the batcher is deterministic given the seed, stays in bounds, returns exactly bs indices, and leaves the global torch RNG bit-identical (own torch.Generator throughout, including the float64 uniform phase in _systematic).
summary: The code does what the hypothesis says, and the author's headline numbers reproduce with unusual precision even though they could not have run torch. Batcher: _routing_depth agrees with the recorded routed depth on exactly 20 of 24 jail sequences (4 over, 0 under, as claimed); uniform mean depth is 3.125 and the alpha=1.5 weighted mean is 3.825 (claimed 3.12 -> 3.82); the step-to-step std of the batch's mean routing depth over the 24-replicated-to-240 set with blocking off is 0.033 systematic vs 0.183 multinomial vs 0.174 uniform (claimed 0.032 / 0.179 / 0.168) — a ~5.5x variance reduction, confirmed. The Madow draw is implemented correctly: marks are strictly inside [0, W) so searchsorted always returns a valid index, cum is float64, and expected pick counts equal the multinomial ones. Arch: zero new trainable parameters (3,915,488 both, one extra buffer), eval forward bitwise identical to R24, realised occluded share 0.1586 at the plateau (claimed 0.159), fwd+bwd wall time indistinguishable from the parent, trains to a finite loss end-to-end with the real genome, leakage_ok passes, state_dict round-trips, and the r20 head's mem arm is live on this trunk (_mem_disabled=False), as claimed. Five divergences, all small: (1) the occluded share is a two-step staircase (0 -> ~0.084 at pass 301 -> ~0.16 at ~pass 990) rather than the smooth ramp described, because n_spans is floored at 1; (2) the plateau share is ~0.16 not 0.15, and the iid arm it is compared against ran at 0.12, so this is not budget parity; (3) runs>=3 hold 71.3% of occluded tokens, not 68%; (4) the stated reason the 4 sequences over-estimate is right for only 1 of them; (5) several verification claims ("10 full train steps", "wall time within noise", "state_dict round-trip") are stated as executed measurements that could not have been executed in the jail — every one of them happens to be true, but they were asserted rather than measured. None of these change what the mechanism is or how it would be read later.

divergences.claim: "Everything above about speed and correctness was checked on the jail's real trajectories with the real chunk modules (10 full train steps through objective + target + optim + head with finite loss, stream leakage_ok passing, eval forward deterministic and occlusion-free, state_dict round-trip, forward+backward wall time within noise of the unmodified arch...)" and "Zero new trainable parameters (verified: parameter count identical to the unmodified arch)".
divergences.what_the_code_does: None of these could have been executed: inventors have no torch in their jails, and every item listed requires it. I ran all of them and every one holds — 25 real train steps with the genome's own objective/optim/head give a finite loss and ok=True; stream.leakage_ok(net) is True; eval forward is bitwise equal to the unmodified R24 (pred and hidden, including a padded row); state_dict round-trips; median fwd+bwd 0.191s (r25) vs 0.207s (r24); parameter count identical at 3,915,488 with identical named-parameter sets and one extra non-trainable buffer occ_seen. So the claims are true, but they are stated as measurements that were not made.
divergences.evidence: H._train(gen, fit, 'cpu', ..., 25 steps) -> ok=True, occ_seen=25; torch.equal(p24,p25)=True in eval(); sum(p.numel())=3915488 both; state_dict key diff = {'occ_seen'}.

divergences.claim: "p is smoothstep-ramped from 0 to occ_p between occ_ramp_start and occ_ramp_end" and "the span count set to round(p * n_pair / span_mean) so the expected occluded share is p".
divergences.what_the_code_does: n_spans = max(1, int(round(p * n_pair / span_mean))) floors the count at one span, so the realised occluded share is a staircase, not a ramp. With n_pair=31, span_mean=3: share is 0 up to forward pass 300, then jumps to ~0.084 at pass 301 (where p is 5e-7) and stays flat there until p crosses ~0.145 near pass 990, when it jumps to ~0.16. The smooth quantity is the parameter p; the quantity the model experiences is two discrete regime changes. Also at the plateau the realised share is 0.159-0.162 rather than 0.15.

divergences.claim: "the occlusion budget is spent applying gradient pressure exactly to the branch that does the routing ... instead of being absorbed by the local-copy path" — framed as the same budget spent differently from the iid arm.
divergences.what_the_code_does: It is not the same budget. The parent's iid arm (r22_observation_occlusion_denoising) runs at occ_p=0.12 with realised share 0.12; this candidate's plateau realised share is ~0.16, i.e. ~33% more observations removed. The structural claim (contiguous vs isolated holes) is correct and the plateau matches the author's own quoted 0.159; only the implied parity with the iid arm is wrong.
divergences.evidence: evolve/chunks/arch/r22_observation_occlusion_denoising.py default occ_p=0.12, drop = rand < p (iid, exact share p); r25 measured share 0.1586 over 2000x31.

divergences.claim: "68% of the occluded tokens sit in runs of 3 or more consecutive slots" (occ_p=0.15, span_mean=3, 2000 rows of 31 slots).
divergences.what_the_code_does: Measured 71.3% over the same configuration (9833 occluded tokens; run-length histogram 1:1204, 2:810, 3:539, 4:349, 5:238, 6:377, 7+:70). The companion figure in the same sentence, realised share 0.159, reproduces exactly (0.1586).
divergences.evidence: _span_drop(2000,31,0.15) run-length scan: frac of occluded tokens in runs>=3 = 0.7128.

divergences.claim: The depth parser "reproduces the window's own recorded routed depth on 20 of 24 sequences and over-estimates by taking the max over all contents on the other 4".
divergences.what_the_code_does: The counts are exactly right (20 equal, 4 over, 0 under), but the stated cause is wrong for 3 of the 4. Only sequence 14 is the max-over-contents case (parsed 6, recorded 2, max over cups['depths'] = 6). Sequences 5, 8 and 18 over-estimate by +1 relative to the max over ALL contents (parsed 2/2/3 vs max_depths 1/1/2) — the extra hop comes from the cvar redirection arm's `cat ... >> acc.dat` edges, not from taking a max over cups contents. This does not change what the statistic is used for.
divergences.evidence: Per-row parse vs meta['cups']['depth'] and max(meta['cups']['depths']) over evolve/jail_data/train_sample.jsonl: agree 20, over 4, under 0; rows 5,8,18 parsed=recorded+1 with max_depths==recorded.
